column2: Retain events and faithfulness, Sennacherib's repeated arrival, siege of walled cities and stated intention to seize them beforehand. Faithfulness does not become a claim that the subsequent invasion was impossible.
column3: The temporal force of beforehand in the capture verb remains provisional.

column2: Retain Hezekiah's recognition of arrival and the enemy's face set toward war on Jerusalem. The bodily orientation expresses intention without inventing a spoken declaration.
Retain consultation with elders and mighty men, blocking spring waters outside the city and their joining in support. Elders is not changed to a different administrative title.

Retain gathering many people, blocked springs and the river dividing through the city, and the concern about abundant water strengthening Assyria's king. Do not substitute a stream through the land for the selected city.
column3: The exact urban/water geography and force of dividing remain unresolved.

column2: Retain Hezekiah's strength, restoration of all demolished wall and towers, a further outer wall, David-city retaining work and many weapons. Do not insert a separate shield category absent here.
column3: Retaining work is a provisional architectural rendering, not a confirmed identification with a named structure.

column2: Retain military commanders, gathering in the Ravine Gate square and speaking to the people's hearts. The selected gate designation is not omitted.
Retain strength, courage, the single terror prohibition, the whole nation with the Assyrian and more with us than with him. More remains plural, not silently turned into an abstract greater power.
Retain plural arms of flesh versus the Lord saving and fighting our war, and the people's courage from Hezekiah's words. The source's number and repeated military image remain.
Retain Sennacherib at Lachish with all the army and servants sent toward Jerusalem, Hezekiah and all Judah there. The location parenthesis does not move the king himself to Jerusalem.
Retain the quoted royal title and challenge about trust while remaining under siege. The threat remains ordinary human speech.
Retain accusation of deception, delivery to death/hunger/thirst and the quoted promise of salvation from Assyria's king. The hostile speaker's claim is not presented as narrator judgment.
Retain the allegation about removal of His altars/high places and worship/incense at this altar. No only is inserted even though the contrast implies concentration of worship.
column3: Capitalized His identifies the deity alleged by the speaker; the allegation need not accurately characterize Hezekiah's reforms.

column2: Retain future will you not learn, the king and his fathers, all peoples, and the emphatic question about national gods' ability. No past-tense knowledge question is substituted.
Retain the elliptical who among the gods, fathers' destruction and the repeated rescue challenge. Do not supply a missing finite predicate as though expressly present.
column3: The relative whom can grammatically attach to the masculine gods rather than neuter nations; the awkward challenge remains provisional pending syntax review.

column2: Retain three warnings against deception/confidence/belief and emphatic inability of national gods followed by your God's future failure in the threat. The father's hand and speaker's hand both remain.
Retain the servants' further words against the Lord and Hezekiah His servant. The two uses of servant have different possessors and are not conflated.
Retain the reproaching letter, explicit God of Israel, national-god analogy and Hezekiah's God with His people. The speaker's singular writing is not changed to the plural servants from verse 16.
Retain singular shouting, Judean language, wall listeners, frightening and bringing down, and the plural purpose of capturing the city. Do not regularize all agents to the same number.
column3: The singular speaker is unexpressed and the precise force of bringing down remains open.

column2: Retain singular speaking against Jerusalem's God as against manufactured national gods. Works of human hands qualifies the comparator gods, not an endorsed characterization of the Lord.
Retain Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz praying and their plural cry to heaven. Isaiah is the selected name here, distinct from Jessias at 26:22.

Retain the Lord's angel, every mighty fighter/ruler/commander destroyed, the king's shameful return and his own descendants striking him in his god's house. No casualty total or assassins' names are imported.
column3: The angel as destroyer and king as returner are contextual subject resolutions; from his body remains a descent idiom.

column2: Retain salvation for Hezekiah and Jerusalem, Sennacherib's named hand, everyone's hand and rest all around. Rest is not changed to a separate guidance verb.
Retain gifts to the Lord and presents to Hezekiah and subsequent exaltation in all nations' eyes. The unnamed exalted person is contextually Hezekiah.
Retain illness to death, prayer, divine hearing and a sign. Do not insert the particular sign or extra years from parallel narratives.
Retain inadequate repayment for divine recompense, lifted heart and wrath on king/Judah/Jerusalem. The source's repayment vocabulary is not replaced by an invented material debt.
column3: Recompense and the unnamed giver require further idiomatic review; the divine reading remains contextual.

column2: Retain humility from the height of his heart, Jerusalem's residents included and no divine wrath in Hezekiah's days. Do not claim the later judgment was permanently canceled.
column3: The shared humility and singular his heart make the inherited syntax awkward and provisional.

column2: Retain exceptionally great wealth/glory, treasuries for precious materials/spices, armories and desirable articles. Places for supplies an understood storage category rather than another explicit building noun.
Retain cities for produce, grain/oil/wine, animal mangers and flock folds. Cities is not silently changed to storehouses.
Retain the repeated cities built for himself, abundant sheep/cattle and the Lord's many possessions given. The repetition is preserved despite overlap with the preceding inventory.
Retain Hezekiah himself closing the upper Gihon outlet and directing waters down toward David city's southwest, then prosperity. Southwest is not changed to west without separate evidence.
Retain Babylonian rulers' ambassadors, inquiry about the wonder on the land and the Lord leaving him for testing and knowing his heart. No extra theological explanation of divine knowledge is added.
Retain remaining deeds and mercy, Isaiah son of Amoz's prophecy and the Judah/Israel royal record. Mercy remains singular rather than an assumed list of pious deeds.

Retain sleep with fathers, burial on the ascent to David's sons' tombs, glory/honor from Judah and Jerusalem and Manasseh's succession. The burial location is not silently changed to the highest tomb.
Retain Manasseh's accession at twelve and fifty-five-year reign in Jerusalem. No maternal name is supplied from a parallel.
Retain evil according to the nations' abominations and their removal before Israel by the Lord. The explanatory comparison is not a new ethnographic description.
Retain rebuilding removed high places, Baal pillars, groves and service/prostration to the whole heavenly army. Pillars is not changed to altars and collective army leads naturally to plural them.
Retain altars inside the Lord's house and the quoted promise of His name in Jerusalem forever. Divine first-person My is ordinary self-reference, not direct archaic address.
Retain heavenly-army altars in both temple courtyards. The explicit two is preserved.
Retain plural children/fire, Gai-banai-ennom, distinct omen/augury/sorcery practices, mediums and enchanters, and multiplied evil provoking anger. No modern supernatural efficacy claim is added.
column3: The five divinatory/cult categories and their English distinctions remain provisional specialist vocabulary.

column2: Retain both carved and cast objects with singular image in apposition, the temple setting, David/Solomon and the promise regarding house/Jerusalem. Do not silently reduce the two object descriptions to one familiar statue phrase.
column3: Whether the coordinated descriptions refer to one image or multiple objects remains open.

column2: Retain no further shaking of Israel's foot from the ancestral land, the obedience condition and law/ordinances/judgments through Moses. The foot image is not replaced with an assured political explanation.
Retain Manasseh misleading Judah/Jerusalem to worse evil than all displaced nations. Both the king's causation and the comparative evaluation remain.
Retain the Lord speaking against Manasseh and his people and their refusal to listen. No unexpressed prophet intermediary is inserted.
Retain divine bringing of Assyrian commanders, seizure in bonds, fetters and transport to Babylon. Bonds is not replaced with hooks or thorns from another textual form.
Retain affliction, seeking the Lord's face and profound humility before the fathers' God. The response is not expanded into a prayer text absent here.
Retain prayer, repeated divine hearing including his cry, restoration to Jerusalem and kingdom and recognition that the Lord is God. The repeated hearing is not removed as redundant.

Retain the external wall, southwest/Gihon/winter-stream route, surrounding gate, Ophla, great height and commanders in all fortified cities. Do not supply Fish Gate to regularize the selected geography.
column3: The participial gate phrase and exact wall route remain unresolved provisional wording.

column2: Retain removal of foreign gods/carved object and altars built on the temple mountain, in Jerusalem and outside the city. No missing throwing verb is inserted before outside the city.
column3: The final location's attachment to building rather than removal remains a provisional reading of the coordination.

column2: Retain restoration of the Lord's altar, salvation and praise offering and command for Judah to serve Israel's God. The singular offering and combined categories remain.
Retain people still at high places yet the Lord as their God. Worshiped is supplied twice to make the selected nominal clauses intelligible.
column3: The supplied action is contextual; the Greek does not expressly use a sacrifice or worship verb in this unit.

column2: Retain deeds, prayer to God, seers speaking in the Lord's name and the unfinished in the accounts phrase continuing into verse 19. Do not insert a royal-book title absent from the selected text.
Retain continuation of prayer, hearing, sins/rebellions, cult sites before turning back and final seers' accounts citation. The two behold/citation fragments remain visibly unresolved.
column3: The cross-verse record citation is syntactically broken; no complete literary acceptance or reconstruction is claimed.

column2: Retain sleep, burial in the garden of his own house and Amon's succession. The garden is not silently replaced with the house itself or a named garden.
Retain Amon's accession at twenty-two and two years in Jerusalem. No further chronology is inferred.
Retain evil following Manasseh's example, sacrifice to all his father's idols and service to them. The repeated father/name references remain for clarity.
Retain failure to humble himself as Manasseh had, explicit his son Amon and multiplied transgression. His in the final clause refers contextually back to Manasseh, not a second son of Amon.
column3: The awkward repeated subject and causal connector remain provisional rather than silently removed.

column2: Retain servants' attack and striking him in his house. The fatal result is clear from succession but no extra killing verb is added here.
Retain the land's people striking the attackers and the repeated people making Josiah king. The same collective acts in retaliation and succession.
